title: Printing in Three Dimensions
passage:
A 3D printer is a machine that creates solid objects from a digital design, building them one thin layer at a time. Although the idea may sound futuristic, the basic process is surprisingly simple to understand.

First, a designer uses computer software to create a three-dimensional model of the object, such as a toy, a tool, or a replacement part. Next, another program called a "slicer" divides that model into hundreds of extremely thin horizontal layers and sends precise instructions to the printer.

The most common type of home printer uses a long strand of plastic called filament. The printer pulls the filament into a heated nozzle, where it melts at roughly two hundred degrees Celsius. The nozzle then moves back and forth, carefully drawing the shape of the first layer onto a flat platform. When that layer cools and hardens, the nozzle rises slightly and draws the next layer on top. Gradually, the layers fuse together until the complete object appears.

This process, called additive manufacturing, differs from traditional methods that cut material away from a larger block. Because the printer adds material only where it is needed, it usually produces less waste.

Today, engineers use 3D printers to produce aircraft parts, doctors use them to design medical models, and students use them to test their inventions. However, printing a large object can still take many hours.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The nozzle then moves back and forth,' which word is a VERB?
options: nozzle
then
back
moves
questions.why: 'Moves' is the action the nozzle performs, so it is the verb.

options: Print the model after you check it.
How long does it take to print a toy?
What an amazing machine this is!
The filament melts in the nozzle.
questions.why: It asks for information and ends with a question mark.

questions.stem: What type of text is this passage?
options: A story about an inventor's adventure
A poem describing modern machines
An informational text explaining a process
A letter asking a school for a printer
questions.why: The passage explains, step by step, how 3D printers make objects.

questions.stem: What happens right AFTER the slicer divides the model into layers?
options: Instructions are sent to the printer
The designer creates the 3D model
The finished object finally appears
The nozzle draws the second layer
questions.why: The slicer 'divides that model… and sends precise instructions to the printer.'

questions.stem: How is additive manufacturing different from traditional methods?
options: It cuts objects from a large block of plastic
It uses no computer design of any kind
It adds layers instead of cutting material away
It always makes objects faster than others
questions.why: The passage contrasts adding material layer by layer with cutting material from a larger block.

questions.stem: The writer says the idea 'may sound futuristic.' What does this phrase suggest?
options: The machine is very old and out of date
The machine is too noisy to use at home
The machine is impossible to understand
The machine seems like something from the future
questions.why: 'Futuristic' means seeming to belong to the future; the writer then says it is actually simple.

questions.stem: Which opinion is BEST supported by the passage?
options: 3D printers are only toys for young children
3D printers are useful in many different jobs
3D printers will soon replace all factories
3D printers are too dangerous for students
questions.why: The last paragraph lists engineers, doctors and students who use them.

questions.stem: Which information in the passage is LEAST complete?
options: How doctors use the medical models they print
What a slicer program does to a model
What the filament in most printers is
How hot the printer's nozzle becomes
questions.why: Doctors are mentioned in one short phrase with no explanation; the others are explained.

options: A printer builds a whole house in a few seconds
A printer makes an object with no design or material
A student prints a small part for a science project
A nozzle melts plastic without using any heat
questions.why: The passage says students use 3D printers to test inventions; the others contradict the facts.

questions.stem: A student's large print takes too long. Based on the passage, which is the BEST solution?
options: Turn off the heated nozzle
Delete the slicer program
Use a block of wood as filament
Print a smaller version of the design
questions.why: The passage says large objects take many hours, so a smaller design prints faster; the others would stop printing.
